content: 1. The proportion of HIV-positive individuals with new or relapsed tuberculosis (TB) who are on antiretroviral therapy (ART) during TB treatment is a critical metric. This includes those who were already on ART or initiated ART during their TB treatment within the reporting period. Data is collected from TB Basic Management Unit (BMU) registers, reconciled with ART registers, and includes information such as TB status, date of enrollment in HIV care, ART start date, and ART follow-up status (e.g., dates ART was stopped, lost to follow-up, restarted, or patient death). Prompt initiation of TB treatment and early ART are essential for reducing mortality. This indicator may reflect the strength of collaboration between national HIV and TB programs. 2. Late ART initiation is defined as the percentage of HIV-positive individuals who begin ART with a baseline CD4 count of less than 200 cells/μL. This is measured by the number of HIV-positive adults initiating ART within the past 12 months with a baseline CD4 count below 200, compared to the total number of HIV-positive adults initiating ART within the same period. Data is sourced from ART registers, including ART start dates and baseline CD4 counts. This indicator highlights delays in ART initiation and serves as a measure of equity in enrollment. The threshold of <200 aligns with the 2016 advanced disease definition by Waldrop et al. 3. ART retention is measured as the percentage of people living with HIV who remain on ART 12 months after initiation (and at subsequent intervals such as 24, 36, 48, and 60 months). This is calculated by dividing the number of individuals alive and on ART at 12 months (or other intervals) by the total number of individuals who initiated ART up to 12 months prior to the reporting period. This includes those who have died, stopped ART, or are lost to follow-up. Data is collected from ART registers and follow-up records, including ART start dates and follow-up status (e.g., dates ART was stopped, lost to follow-up, restarted, or patient death). 4. Viral load suppression is defined as the percentage of people living with HIV on ART who achieve a suppressed viral load (<1000 copies/mL) during the reporting period. This is calculated by dividing the number of individuals with suppressed viral loads by the total number of individuals on ART at the end of the reporting period. Data is sourced from laboratory registers, ART registers, and cross-sectional reports. Viral load suppression is the gold standard for assessing ART adherence and is measured using routine viral load testing. If viral load testing coverage is below 75% of those on ART, results should be interpreted cautiously, as per UNAIDS guidelines. 5. Cotrimoxazole (CTX) prophylaxis coverage is measured as the percentage of HIV-exposed infants who are started on CTX prophylaxis within two months of birth. This is calculated by dividing the number of HIV-exposed infants born in the past 12 months who started CTX within two months by the total number of HIV-positive women who delivered in the same period. Data is collected from HIV-exposed infant (HEI) registers, including date of birth and age at CTX initiation. CTX prophylaxis is essential for reducing opportunistic infections and bacterial infections in HIV-exposed infants and serves as a proxy for HEI follow-up. 6. TB screening coverage in HIV care is defined as the proportion of individuals in HIV care (including prevention of mother-to-child transmission, PMTCT) who were screened for TB in HIV care and treatment settings. This is calculated by dividing the number of HIV-positive individuals enrolled in HIV care in the past 12 months whose TB status was assessed and recorded at their last visit by the total number of HIV-positive individuals enrolled in HIV care within the same period. Data is sourced from ART registers, including TB status, date of enrollment in HIV care, ART start date, and follow-up status. This indicator measures the extent of TB screening coverage in HIV care settings. 7. Early ART initiation for HIV-positive TB patients is measured as the proportion of HIV-positive individuals with new or relapsed TB who start ART within eight weeks of their TB diagnosis. This is calculated by dividing the number of HIV-positive TB patients who started ART within eight weeks of diagnosis by the total number of HIV-positive TB patients detected during the reporting period who were not already on ART. Data is collected from HIV patient cards or ART registers, reconciled with TB registers, and includes ART start dates and TB status. Early ART initiation significantly improves survival and quality of life for TB patients living with HIV, though it may require labor-intensive data collection. 8. Viral load testing coverage is defined as the percentage of individuals on ART who have viral load test results available at 12 months after ART initiation. This is calculated by dividing the number of individuals on ART with viral load test results at 12 months by the total number of individuals alive and on ART at 12 months. Data is sourced from laboratory registers, ART registers, and ART cohort reports, including ART start dates and follow-up status. This indicator measures the extent of viral load testing coverage and excludes individuals without viral load results from the denominator. 9. ART survival is measured as the percentage of people living with HIV who are alive at 12, 24, 36 months, etc., after ART initiation. This is calculated by dividing the number of individuals alive and on ART at these time points by the total number of individuals who initiated ART up to the corresponding time point. The numerator has been revised to include and on ART to ensure consistency with the cohort-based denominator. Data aggregation across service delivery points may be necessary for accurate reporting.
